title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Reference, Customer Requirements, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback
author: Lina Morales
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s canonical guidance for private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem packaging). It covers: reference architectures, on‑prem packaging and deployment artifacts, a customer requirements library (pre‑sales and onboarding checklist), Day‑2 operational practices (monitoring, backups, scaling), and upgrade & rollback procedures. Intended audience: Solutions Engineers, Site Reliability Engineers, Customer Success, and Deployment Engineers.

Goals
- Provide a single reference to reduce variability between customer engagements.
- Reduce deployment time-to-first-request and minimize post-deploy incidents.
- Ensure upgrades are safe, auditable, and reversible.

Scope
- VPC-hosted private control plane + customer-managed inference VPC (typical cloud: AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Fully air-gapped on‑prem packaging (appliance-style) for regulated customers.
- Day‑0 (requirements & packaging), Day‑1 (deployment), and Day‑2 (operations, upgrades, rollback).

Owners & Contacts
- Product Owner: Lina Morales (eng-private-deployments)
- Deployment Lead: Raj Patel (solutions-eng)
- SRE Contact: Evelyn Chen (eng-sre)

Reference Architectures
1) VPC Managed Inference (recommended for most customers)
- Components: Private Control Plane (customer VPC), Inference Fleet (customer subnet with GPU hosts or cloud GPU nodes), Bastion / Jumpbox, NAT & egress rules, KMS integration for keywrap, and optional private S3-like object store for model artifacts.
- Network: Separate inference and control subnets. Minimum CIDR planning: /24 for control plane, /22 for inference nodes (adjust by expected GPU count).
- IAM & RBAC: Use least-privilege roles; recommended role mappings: control-plane-admin, inference-node-provisioner, read-only-audit.
- SLOs and targets: 99.9% control-plane availability SLA; 95th percentile inference tail latency target based on profile (e.g., <120ms for 128-token generation on small models).

2) On‑prem (air‑gapped) Appliance
- Components: Pre-packaged container images, local registry, hardware compatibility list (HCL), local KMS/HSM integration, NFS or distributed filesystem for artifacts, and an optional management VM for metrics ingestion.
- Packaging: OVA/ISO for VM-based installs or tarball of images + helm charts for K8s-based installs.
- Minimum HW: 2 control VMs (4 vCPU, 16GB RAM), inference hosts: 1+ GPUs (A10/A100 equivalent), 500GB root disk + 2TB model storage per GPU depending on model mix.

On‑Prem Packaging & Delivery
- Delivery artifacts: signed manifest.json, image checksums (SHA256), onboarding playbook, and offline package containing: docker images (.tar), helm charts, and post-install verification scripts.
- Verification: All images must be signed; provide verification CLI:

  ```bash
  # verify images and manifest
  redwood-verify --manifest manifest.json --signature manifest.sig
  ```

Customer Requirements Library (Pre‑sales / Onboarding Checklist)
- Network & Connectivity
  - VPC CIDR, subnets for control & inference, NAT/gateway details, and firewall ACLs.
  - Egress policy: list allowed outbound endpoints for registry or management plane (if not fully air-gapped).
- Identity & Secrets
  - KMS/HSM details, service principal or IAM role mapping, certificate signing authority, and rotation policy.
- Storage & Artifacts
  - Object store access (S3-compatible), required bucket policies, retention policy, and expected model artifact sizes.
- Compute
  - GPU instance types or on‑prem GPU models, expected concurrency, and peak qps.
- Compliance & Security
  - Data residency, encryption at rest and in transit requirements, audit logging S3/GEL/ELK endpoints, and necessary SOC/ISO evidence.
- Change & Maintenance
  - Maintenance windows, patching cadence, and contact roster for emergency change approvals.

Day‑1 Deployment Checklist (High level)
1) Pre-checks (run with customer)
  - Validate network CIDRs and firewall rules.
  - Confirm service accounts and KMS access.
  - Confirm image access and checksum verification.
2) Install control plane
  - Apply helm charts to target cluster or install control-plane VMs.
  - Configure control-plane endpoints, TLS certs, and DNS entries.
3) Provision inference nodes
  - Label nodes with gpu=true and apply node taints.
  - Deploy runtime agent and verify GPU drivers and CUDA versions.
4) Smoke tests
  - Run end-to-end inference smoke tests: model pull, tokenize, generate, and metrics emission.
  - Verify monitoring dashboards ingest metrics (Prometheus) and logs (Fluentd/Vector).

Day‑2 Operations
- Monitoring & Alerts
  - Metrics to track: token/s, qps, tail latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), GPU utilization, host memory, and KV cache hit rate.
  - Recommended alert thresholds: GPU memory usage > 90% (warning), p99 latency > baseline+250ms (critical), model pull failures > 5/min (warning).
  - Dashboards: per-customer per-model latency, cost breakdown, and tracing for top 10 slow requests.
- Backups & Disaster Recovery
  - Control plane backups: etcd snapshots (if k8s), DB dumps every 24h, and offsite replication.
  - Model artifacts: replicate to cross-region or customer-provided backup store.
  - Recovery RTO/RPO targets: RTO 2 hours for control plane, RPO 1 hour for metrics.
- Scaling & Autoscaling
  - Autoscaling policy examples: scale-out when p95 token latency > 200ms for 5m or GPU utilization > 70% for 10m.
  - Graceful draining: cordon node, wait for in-flight requests (configurable 30‑120s), then terminate.
- Patch management
  - Security patches: monthly scheduled patches during agreed maintenance window. Critical CVEs: immediate mitigation plan and possible emergency window.

Upgrade & Rollback Procedures (Approved flow)
1) Pre-upgrade (gating checks)
  - Verify canary tests and automated evals for the new runtime/model package against a canonical test harness.
  - Verify backup completion and snapshot integrity (etcd snapshot, DB dump, model artifact versioning).
  - Stakeholder sign-off: customer admin and Redwood deployment owner.
2) Canary deployment
  - Strategy: route 5‑10% of traffic to canary nodes (isolated node pool).
  - Monitoring: track error rate, latency, and token-level regressions against baseline prompts.
  - Evaluation period: 30‑120 minutes depending on traffic and complexity.
3) Gradual rollout
  - If canary is healthy, ramp traffic in increments (25% → 50% → 100%) over configured windows (15‑60 minutes between steps).
  - Monitor rollback indicators (errors, latency, cost impact).
4) Rollback (automated and manual)
  - Automated rollback: if error rate > 2% absolute increase or p99 latency > baseline + 400ms for two consecutive windows, promote automated rollback to previous stable revision.
  - Manual rollback steps:
    1. Cordon new nodes and stop traffic routing.
    2. Re-deploy previous image revision from signed artifact store.
    3. Validate smoke tests and traffic routing.
    4. Run postmortem and record RCA; notify customer and internal stakeholders within SLA.

Upgrade Playbook (step-by-step)
1) Prepare release artifacts and manifest with SHA256 checksums.
2) Create a release ticket and schedule maintenance window (if required).
3) Run pre-upgrade test suite on staging and canary harness.
4) Execute canary deployment; observe for evaluation period.
5) Roll out gradually or trigger rollback.
6) After full rollout, run post-upgrade verification checklist and update runbook with lessons learned.

Post-incident and RCAs
- All upgrade failures that trigger rollback require a P0/P1 style incident report and a 72-hour initial RCA. Longer-term mitigation should be tracked in Jira and linked in the related_pages field.

Operational Playbooks (short links)
- Node GPU OOM: cordon node, collect diagnostics (/var/log/redwood/runtime.log), rotate logs, and reprovision.
- Control-plane DB corruption: restore etcd snapshot (timestamped) and rehydrate services.
- Model artifact corruption: re-pull from signed repository; validate checksums.

Sample Terraform / K8s Snippets
- Example node taint (k8s):
  ```yaml
  spec:
    taints:
    - key: "redwood/inference"
      value: "true"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
  ```
- Example terraform snippet for subnet creation (AWS):
  ```hcl
  resource "aws_subnet" "inference" {
    vpc_id = var.vpc_id
    cidr_block = "10.0.8.0/22"
    tags = { Name = "redwood-inference-nodes" }
  }
  ```

Security & Compliance Considerations
- Audit logging: all control-plane changes must be logged to the customer’s audit store for 365+ days (configurable).
- Key management: prefer customer-managed KMS; rotate keys every 90 days.
- Access controls: enable MFA for control-plane admin roles and require Just‑In‑Time (JIT) approvals for emergency changes.

Appendix A — Ports and Endpoints (minimum)
- Control-plane API: TCP 8443 (HTTPS)
- Metrics (Prometheus scrape): TCP 9100/9090 internal
- Model artifact pull (S3-compatible): TCP 443
- Runtime grpc endpoint (inference): TCP 50051

Appendix B — SLOs & Alerting Templates
- Control plane availability: 99.9% monthly
- Inference tail latency: p95 < 250ms for targeted models; p99 < 600ms
- Alert template example: subject: "[ALERT] {customer} inference p99 latency > threshold". Body: include timeseries snapshot, affected model, node list, and last deployment hash.

Appendix C — Onboarding Timeline (example)
- Week 0: Kickoff, collect requirements, and sign-off on HCL and network.
- Week 1: Deliver packaging, run Day‑1 deployment with customer staff.
- Week 2: Validation, load testing, and SLA sign-off.
